acceptance: A scheduled refresh run fails with a message naming the still-open previous refresh pull request.
Nothing else about the gate or the workflow's commits changed.
context: Filed 2026-11-20 from the adversarial review of the scale-factor and TPC-DI remediation work (PRs #4298-#4385 and benchbox-site #178-#210).
description:
## Problem
Scheduled baseline refresh pull requests stall unnoticed: fast-tier #3928, #4066 and #4283 were opened by the Monday schedule and closed unmerged days later; medium-shard #4284 has been open since 2026-11-16 and now conflicts. Both come from .github/workflows/fast-duration-baseline-refresh.yml. Each was marked too large to review and waited for a stand-in nobody posted.

## Owner decision
Answer: "leave the identity alone. Add only a visible failure when a scheduled refresh opens while the previous one is still open." Source: owner's answer in the choice dialog, 2026-11-20. The earlier scope of this item (a `reproduce` check, a staleness warning, a refresh cadence) was not chosen and is removed from it; nothing replaces it.

## Change
In the refresh workflow, before opening a new refresh pull request, look for an open pull request from the same refresh family (fast-tier, medium-shard). If one exists, fail the run with a message naming it and saying it needs the owner's stand-in or closing. Re-check the workflow on current develop first.

## Decision gates
No change to the gate, the baseline, the thresholds, the commit identity, `.github/soundness-paths.txt` or `.github/inert-paths.txt`. Whether the failing run still opens the new pull request is shown to the owner in the pull request body before arming; default: it does not open a second one.

## Verification rubric
Pass: workflow lint passes; a test or a dry run of the step with a fixture list of open pull requests shows it fails and names the open one, and passes when none is open; the workflow's existing tests pass.

## Guardrails (accepted by the owner, 2026-11-20)
The agent never posts a stand-in review, resolves a review thread, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. It arms with `make pr-arm` once per pull request and reports the result. Subagents are read-only. Any limit, default, threshold or label text is shown to the owner before it is committed. A blocked step stops this item; the agent moves to the next item and does not work around the block.
